3. The defendant-opposite parties upon prayer for dismissal of the suit stated that the suit land belonged to government and it was leased out to the plaintiff-petitioners wrong-fully since the said land is high laying in nature and do not contain cultivable land and that the government has title and possession over the said land and the said khatian was cancelled on 25-3-2003 and the lease settlement was cancelled properly by issuing notice to the leasee plaintiffs. It is stated that the suit is not maintainable in this form and nature and it is barred by limitation and also stated other grounds in respect of dismissal of the plaintiffs's suit. 

 6. The trial court examined 2 witnesses from the plaintiff-petitioners' side and also examined 1 witness from the defend ant-opposite parties. The plaintiff-petitioners exhibited before the court the registered kabuliyat which was executed between Bangladesh Government and the plaintiff-petitioners and that the said kabuliyat was registered upon a proceeding of the government office. The plaintiff-petitioners also exhibited the mutated khatian against the suit land in their names and rent receipts of the said land were also produced before the learned court. 

 8. During trial, the plaintiff-petitioners proved their case by deposition of witnesses, by exhibits of registered kabuliyat, evidences of payment of rents to the government and suit khatian before the court.
